title: Wind Farm development/ Air Force missile fields

communications.subject: Montana Freedom of Information Act Request: Wind Farm development/ Air Force missile fields
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Montana Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Attn Ben Brouwer, Energy Bureau Chief

1. A map of the area in Montana that is off-limits to wind farms due to Air Force restrictions on wind turbine development within 2 nautical miles of intercontinental ballistic missile silos overseen by Malmstrom Air Force Vase. Or, if not that, the inverse – a map of the state where wind farms are allowed (a map that would presumably show a large exclusion area over the panhandle where silos are located).

2. Any records on how many proposed wind farms (such as the Grizzly Wind farm)  were impacted by the Air Force's 2 nautical mile restriction on airspace around missile silos, including any records detailing their expected power generation and how many turbines they would have included.

3. Any studies or records on the expected socioeconomic impact of those wind farms (such as Grizzly Wind) would have had on communities in the area.

4. Any records on average, market-rate leasing fees that landowners receive when leasing land for turbines.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Taylor Barnes

title: Ibrahim Aqil

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Ibrahim Aqil
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552, I am writing to request records concerning IBRAHIM AQIL, also known as "Tahsin," "Abed Ahmad," and "Abu Suja."
 
This request follows FOIPA Request No. 1647643-000, which the Bureau closed on June 4, 2025, after a standard search of the Central Records System (main and reference entity records)
returned no records responsive to that request. That response invited me to submit "additional information pertaining to the subject of [the] request" so that an additional search could be conducted. This request provides that additional information and asks the Bureau to conduct a new, expanded search on that basis.
 
ADDITIONAL IDENTIFYING AND BACKGROUND INFORMATION
 
Ibrahim Aqil was, until his death, a senior Hezbollah military commander and member of Hezbollah's Jihad Council, and has been publicly linked by the U.S. government to activity squarely within the FBI's counterterrorism mission:
 
  - Aqil was identified by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, in a July 21, 2015 designation under Executive Order 13582, as acting for or on behalf of Hezbollah.
 
  - Aqil was designated by the U.S. Department of State as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist under Executive Order 13224, as amended, effective September 10, 2019.
 
  - The U.S. government's Rewards for Justice program — administered by the State Department in coordination with U.S. law enforcement and intelligence agencies, including the FBI — offered a reward of up to $7 million for information on Aqil.
 
  - Public reporting attributes to Aqil a role, in the early-to-mid 1980s, in the Islamic Jihad Organization cell tied to the April 1983 bombing of the U.S. Embassy in Beirut (63 killed, including 17 Americans) and the October 1983 bombing of the U.S. Marine Corps barracks in Beirut (241 U.S. servicemembers killed) — attacks that were the subject of extensive FBI and U.S. government investigation, and reporting also links him to the taking of American hostages in Lebanon during that period.
 
  - Aqil was reportedly killed in an Israeli airstrike in Beirut on September 20, 2024, an event widely covered in domestic and international press.
 
Given a formal U.S. terrorist designation, a multimillion-dollar federal reward for information on his whereabouts, and his public association with attacks that killed dozens of Americans and prompted a major federal investigation, I believe it is likely that the FBI's Central Records System — including but not limited to files maintained by FBI Headquarters, relevant field offices, and Legal Attaché offices, as well as Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) records — contains records responsive to this request that a standard main-entity-only search would not necessarily surface, particularly reference-entity records connecting Aqil to related investigative files, watch-list or terrorist-designation processing, or the Rewards for Justice program.
 
RECORDS REQUESTED
 
Please search for and produce all records, of any kind, mentioning, referencing, or otherwise relating to Ibrahim Aqil (and the aliases above), including but not limited to:
 
  1. Investigative files, main and reference entity records, indices entries, and 302s or equivalent reports referencing Aqil, under any of the names/aliases listed above;
 
  2. Records relating to Aqil's designation as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist and any predecessate or related Treasury/OFAC designation;
 
  3. Records relating to the Rewards for Justice reward offer concerning Aqil, including any FBI role in vetting, verifying, or acting on tips submitted in connection with that reward;
 
  4. Records relating to the 1983 U.S. Embassy Beirut bombing and/or the 1983 U.S. Marine Corps barracks bombing in Beirut that reference Aqil by name or alias;
 
  5. Any records generated, updated, or closed out following Aqil's reported death on September 20, 2024.
 
INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING SEARCH
 
As required by relevant case law (e.g., Weisberg v. DOJ, 705 F.2d 1344, 1351 (D.C. Cir. 1983); Valencia-Lucena v. U.S. Coast Guard, 180 F.3d 321, 325 (D.C. Cir. 1999)), the FBI must conduct a
search reasonably calculated to uncover all responsive records, including both main and reference entity records given the additional information provided above, and must follow any clear leads it discovers to other systems or record locations. If any potentially responsive records were destroyed, transferred to NARA, or otherwise unavailable, please identify that fact and the applicable disposition authority per FOIPA Addendum Part 1.
 
EXEMPTIONS AND SEGREGABILITY
 
Per the foreseeable-harm standard at 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(8)(A), please withhold information only where disclosure would reasonably be expected to harm an interest protected by a specific exemption, or where disclosure is prohibited by law. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of any record, and identify the specific exemption(s) claimed for each redaction or withholding.

FEES AND FORMAT

I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.
